jobs.description:
Executive Director RCFE

Pay Range: $160,000 - $170,000

Ivy Park at Hayward
is a premier senior living community located in Hayward, California and managed by Oakmont Management Group.

Based in Irvine, California, Oakmont Management Group is a recognized leader in senior living, operating 110+ communities under the Oakmont Senior Living and Ivy Living brands. We are the #1 operator in California and a top ten operator in the United States, serving thousands of seniors across California, Nevada, Colorado, and Hawaii. With strong momentum and continued expansion, we are actively growing into new markets.

The Executive Director
is responsible for the efficient operations and overall management and direction of the day-to-day functions of their Community in accordance with property policies and procedures, current standards, guidelines, and regulations. They will hire, evaluate, coordinate, monitor performance, schedule, and supervise staff in accordance with company policy. The Executive Director is also responsible for achieving and maintaining budgeted occupancy; achieving and maintaining budgetary compliance; professionally representing the property to the community and the Corporation, and creating a supportive and enjoyable lifestyle for the residents.

Prefer five (5) years of experience supervising and managing employees
Able to operate a personal computer and be proficient in MS Office programs (Word, Excel, etc.)
Knowledge of and/or ability to learn the theory and practice of assisted living and dementia care
Able to work with seniors and patiently interact with cognitively impaired individuals
Able to be flexible, adapt and respond to change, make decisions in stressful situations, and prioritize tasks and projects.
Able to process information and apply common sense understanding to follow and carry out written or oral instructions.
Able to analyze, solve and respond to problems or concerns.
Able to count and perform moderately complex math problems, read and understand budgets and other financial reports/statements
Able to explain ideas and communicate complex ideas to a wide audience (employees, residents, family members, governmental agencies, public, etc) both in writing and verbally

jobs.description:
Job Description

Job Summary:

Leads the implementation and ongoing management of foodservice systems that support patient dining and retail operations. Oversees the implementation and optimization of digital platforms for menu management, patient meal selection entry, patient meal delivery, and point-of-sale integration to production systems to ensure accuracy, efficiency, and data-driven decision-making. Partners with IT network teams, security teams, integration teams, clinical nutrition leadership, culinary leadership, and procurement leadership to align systems with organizational goals and regulatory standards. Ensures seamless interoperability across technology platforms and supports continuous improvement through system enhancements, automation, and analytics. Continualy enhances the patient and guest experience through reliable, user-centered technology solutions that advance operational performance and service quality.

Supports and implements technology initiatives that enhance food service operations and patient experience that align with enterprise strategies and evolving healthcare needs. Coordinates the implementation and optimization of systems—such as automation, analytics, and digital ordering platforms—to improve decision-making and service delivery. Ensures resources, budgets, and timelines are effectively managed to achieve performance goals. Anticipates emerging risks and opportunities, adapting strategies to maintain resilience and scalability. Provides inputs and helps develope policies and standards that advance modernization efforts and may influence system-wide practices. Serves as a trusted subject matter expert and change agent, fostering collaboration across food service, IT, and operational teams to deliver transformative outcomes. Manages day to day food service information systems including the electronic health record integration with the kitchen software and hardware, related call center management systems as well as retail point of sale integration with ordering solutions and signage platforms. Performance will be assessed on ability to improve digital adoption of technologies by customers and patients, the reliability and operability of foodservice technology, ability to lead upgrades within established budgets and timelines, and manage to labor budget.

Department Description

The UCSF Health Department of Nutrition and Food Services is a high-performing, nationally recognized food and nutrition service operation. The department comprises three divisions:

Food Service: Includes room service–style patient dining, retail food operations such as cafés and quick-service coffee outlets, a large-scale catering and conference services program, and supporting entities including culinary services, food procurement, and a business office.

Nutrition Services: Provides inpatient and outpatient nutrition care for adults and pediatrics and operates an accredited dietetic internship program.

Retail Services: UCSF Health’s gift and specialty shops.

These entities are primarily based across UCSF Health’s six hospital campuses and affiliated clinics throughout the Bay Area. The department employs approximately 400 FTEs and manages an overall operating budget of $50 million.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in related area and / or 4 years of equivalent experience working with foodservice technology systems.
At least three years of experience in food services
3 years of project management experience of small or large projects that includes critical thinking, and ability to multi-task and ensure effective time management.
Thorough knowledge in food service operations and sanitation regulations.
Thorough verbal and written communication skills in the English language, including active listening, dynamic flexibility, and critical thinking, and ability to multi-task and ensure effective time management.
Excellent decision making and reasoning skills, and excellent ability to develop original ideas to solve problems and perform operations analysis and quality control analysis.
Excellent and effective interpersonal and work leadership skills to provide guidance to all levels of personnel. Strong computer application skills.

Preferred Qualifications

3 years of experience in writing proposal that includes decision making skills, ability to develop original ideas to solve problems and perform operations analysis and quality control analysis.
At least two years of experience working with teams larger than 20 people demonstration effective interpersonal and leadership skills to provide guidance to all levels of personnel.
Ability to provide two examples of perform operations analysis and quality control analysis.
ServSafe® Food Protection Manager Certification or equivalent food protection manager certification recognized by the state of California. Valid certificate must be on file in department.

About Us

About UCSF

The University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) is a leading university dedicated to promoting health worldwide through advanced biomedical research, graduate-level education in the life sciences and health professions, and excellence in patient care. It is the only campus in the 10-campus UC system dedicated exclusively to the health sciences. We bring together the world’s leading experts in nearly every area of health. We are home to five Nobel laureates who have advanced the understanding of cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, aging and stem cells.

Pride Values

UCSF is a diverse community made of people with many skills and talents. We seek candidates whose work experience or community service has prepared them to contribute to our commitment to professionalism, respect, integrity, diversity and excellence – also known as our PRIDE values .

In addition to our PRIDE values, UCSF is committed to equity – both in how we deliver care as well as our workforce. We are committed to building a broadly diverse community, nurturing a culture that is welcoming and supportive, and engaging diverse ideas for the provision of culturally competent education, discovery, and patient care. Join us to find a rewarding career contributing to improving healthcare worldwide.

jobs.description:
How many people can answer the question, "What do you do for a living?" with the answer, "I help find cures for cancer."
At Blood Cancer United, employees take our mission seriously. Whether you work in one of our regions, are an accountant at the national office or a specialist in our Information Resource Center, you work each day on making our bold goal a reality: to enable patients with blood cancer to gain more than one million years of life by 2040.
Join us and give new meaning to the word, "job."

Summary:
The Director of Philanthropy is a front-line fundraiser responsible for securing major gifts within a designated market. This role focuses on managing a portfolio of high-capacity donors and prospects to secure funding for our mission. The Director will implement strategic cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship activities to meet and exceed revenue goals, relentlessly pursuing cancer cures.

Portfolio Management & Major Gift Fundraising 

Manage a portfolio of qualified major gift prospects, with a focus on donors capable of giving $10,000 or more.

Accountable for achieving an annual revenue target by creating and implementing personalized fundraising strategies. 
Conduct a significant number of meaningful donor interactions, including face-to-face visits, to advance relationships and secure gifts. 
Prepare and present compelling proposals and materials for major gift solicitations. 

Pipeline Development & Strategy Execution  

In partnership with the Sr. Director, actively build and grow the major gift pipeline by identifying new prospects from various channels (e.g., events, direct mail, volunteer networks). 
Utilize internal analytics and research tools to qualify prospects and develop strategic engagement plans. 
Collaborate with national partners to identify opportunities for Principal Gifts, Planned Giving, and Foundation support within the portfolio. 
Ensure timely and accurate tracking of all donor interactions and pipeline movement in Salesforce. 

  Collaboration & Mission Advancement 

 Partner with Executive Directors, regional staff, and volunteer leaders to identify donor prospects and create a seamless donor experience. 
Serve as a knowledgeable and passionate representative of the mission, effectively communicating our impact and funding priorities to donors. 
Participate in mission-centered cultivation events and activities to engage prospects and donors. 
Maintain a working knowledge of the Blood Cancer United mission and programs to promote organizational initiatives.

Bachelor’s Degree required. 
5-7+ years of fundraising experience, with a demonstrated track record of success in individual major gift fundraising.

Experience managing a portfolio of donors, including personally identifying, cultivating, and soliciting five- and six-figure gifts. 
Proficiency in Salesforce or similar CRM database. 
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

As the Executive Director
, you will oversee all strategic, financial, and operational aspects of the ProAmpac Employee Assistance Fund (PEAF). You will carry out the vision of the organization, leading efforts to scale the fund globally, engage our workforce, and ensure the fund's long-term sustainability.

Whether you are navigating compliance, collaborating with the Board of Directors, or visiting our manufacturing sites to raise awareness, your leadership will directly support employees when they need it most.

Strategic Leadership & Global Expansion

Expand Our Reach: Lead the expansion of the fund to international locations and newly acquired manufacturing sites, adapting processes to respect regional HR policies and practices.

Reporting: Prepare and deliver program metrics, financial updates, and impact reports for board meetings.
Fundraising: Design and champion creative fundraising initiatives, including annual donor campaigns, employee payroll deduction programs, and special events.

Education: Bachelor’s degree in Nonprofit Management, Business Administration, Human Resources, or a closely related field preferred.
Experience: Proven experience managing charitable programs, foundation grants, or corporate employee assistance funds (required).

Financial Acumen: Strong program administration skills with experience in budgeting, financial reporting, and donor tracking.

Key Competencies

Strategic Leadership: Ability to think long-term and transition ideas into highly structured, compliant global programs.
Empathetic Communication: Exceptional relationship-building skills to connect with plant floor employees, executive leadership, and board members alike.
Nonprofit Governance: Deep understanding of regulatory compliance, IRS guidelines for charitable funds, and board administration.

Metrics for Success

Growth in active employee participation and total recurring contributions.
Awareness increases across all manufacturing and corporate sites.
Efficiency in processing and distributing critical grants equitably.
Seamless onboarding of global sites and newly acquired locations into the program.

Travel & Physical Requirements

Travel: Ability to travel 20-25% to various corporate and manufacturing locations to promote fund awareness and build community relationships.

Chief Executive Officer (CEO) – Recovery Works Martinsville

Make an Impact. Lead with Innovation. Transform Lives.

network, is seeking a Chief Executive Officer who is ready to combine operational excellence with a deep-seated passion for recovery.

Located in the rolling hills of Morgan County, Martinsville offers a high quality of life with a perfect balance of rural peace and urban accessibility.

Gateway to Southern Indiana: Enjoy the scenic beauty of nearby Brown County State Park and the outdoor recreation that defines Morgan County.
The Best of Both Worlds: Located just 30 miles from the professional pulse of Indianapolis and 20 miles from the academic and cultural vibrancy of Bloomington (IU), Martinsville is perfectly positioned for commuting and professional networking.

Hear From Our Patients

"I walked in here lost and terrified. The leadership and the staff gave me a roadmap when I didn't think I had a destination left. They didn't just treat my addiction; they saw me
." — PTC Patient

Strategic Vision: Drive the facility’s growth through innovative clinical programming and community partnerships across Morgan, Monroe, and Marion Counties.
Operational Excellence: Lead daily operations with a focus on patient safety, high-quality clinical outcomes, and fiscal responsibility.
Mentorship: Cultivate a high-performing leadership team grounded in Pinnacle’s core values of innovation and ownership.
Compliance: Ensure the facility exceeds all Indiana Division of Mental Health and Addiction (DMHA) and CARF regulatory standards.

What You Bring

A Master’s Degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, or a Human Services field (preferred).
A minimum of 5 years of senior-level management experience in a behavioral health or residential treatment setting.
An innovative spirit and the ability to lead a dedicated team in a mission-critical environment.

We take care of those who take care of our patients. Our package includes:

Competitive Salary: With performance-based bonus incentives.

Future Security: 401(k) with a generous company match.
Time to Recharge: 18 days of PTO plus paid holidays.
Education: Tuition scholarships and STAR LRP loan repayment programs.

Substance use disorder is a relentless challenge in Indiana, but it is one we meet with hope and innovation. You will work closely with the Board of Directors and Leadership Team to strengthen organizational effectiveness, sustainability, and impact.

You will serve as a prominent public representative, helping shape conversations around peer support, crisis intervention, and community-centered services.

Executive Director
to join our community.
